flaws.title: Trailing call uses the first call's arguments
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to remember the arguments or `this` for the delayed call, or asks for the whole debounce.
flaws.wrongClaim: Save the arguments only when the timer is not yet running (the first call of a burst) and later calls just restart the timer, describing that as the standard behavior.
flaws.correctBehavior: The trailing call must use the arguments and `this` of the most recent call. Update them on every call.

flaws.title: Leading+trailing fires twice for a single call
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how the leading and trailing options should work together, or how to implement leading.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say that with both enabled the function runs on the leading edge and then again on the trailing edge, always, and implement it that way.
flaws.correctBehavior: The trailing call only happens if the function was called again during the burst. A single call must call fn exactly once.

flaws.title: cancel() leaves the burst open
flaws.trigger: The learner asks for cancel() or flush(), or how to clean up state.
flaws.wrongClaim: Implement cancel as just clearing the timer with clearTimeout, and leave the stored timer id and pending arguments alone.
flaws.correctBehavior: cancel must also reset the timer id (so a new burst is detected and leading fires again) and drop the pending arguments.

flaws.title: Backoff off by one (factor ** n)
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to compute the retry delay or exponential backoff.
flaws.wrongClaim: Use `baseMs * factor ** attempt` where attempt counts tries starting from 1, and describe the first delay as baseMs times the factor.
flaws.correctBehavior: The first wait is baseMs, so the exponent is n - 1: baseMs * factor ** (n - 1), capped by maxMs.

flaws.title: attempts counted as retries, one try too many
flaws.trigger: The learner asks for the retry loop, or how to decide when to stop retrying.
flaws.wrongClaim: Stop when the try number is greater than attempts (n <= attempts keeps going), so attempts: 3 gives four tries, and describe attempts as the number of retries.
flaws.correctBehavior: attempts is the total number of tries. Retry only while n < attempts.

flaws.title: cancel() only clears the timer
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to implement cancel() for retry.
flaws.correctBehavior: cancel must also set a cancelled flag that the task callback checks, because a try that is already in flight can still call back later and would schedule a retry or call the user's callback.

flaws.title: Trusts the task to call cb once
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to make retry robust against tasks that call cb more than once, or about calling the callback exactly once.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say a well-behaved task calls cb once, so no guard is needed in retry.
flaws.correctBehavior: Guard each try with an answered flag, because a task that calls cb twice with errors would schedule duplicate retries.
